title: GsOQDC: A GUI-Driven Interactive Framework for End-to-End Simulation of Optical Quantum Data Centers
authors: Seyed Navid Elyasi, Sima Bahrani, Rui Wang, Dimitra Simeonidou, Paolo Monti, Rui Lin
abstract: We present GsOQDC, an open-source graphical framework integrating optical-network design, distributed quantum-circuit compilation, scheduling, and DES-based remote-gate simulation, enabling end-to-end cross-layer evaluation of entanglement-resource dynamics and system-level performance in Optical Quantum Data Centers.
summary: The paper introduces GsOQDC, an open-source GUI framework designed to simulate end-to-end operations in Optical Quantum Data Centers (OQDCs). It integrates quantum circuit design, network topology definition, compilation, and scheduling into a single platform. This allows researchers to quantitatively evaluate how physical network impairments affect the performance of distributed quantum algorithms.
main_problem: There is a lack of an integrated environment to evaluate the end-to-end behavior of distributed quantum applications, especially concerning the interaction between quantum computation and optical network resources in Quantum Data Centers (QDCs).
main_result: The GsOQDC framework enables quantitative analysis of how optical network characteristics influence application-level performance metrics like fidelity, overhead, and job execution time in future Optical Quantum Data Centers.
method: It utilizes a graphical, open-source framework integrating quantum circuit modeling, optically switched interconnection design, distributed compilation, scheduling, and a Discrete-Event Simulation (DES) engine.
model_or_system: The system modeled is an Optical Quantum Data Center (OQDC), consisting of multiple interconnected Quantum Processing Units (QPUs) linked by optical networks. The framework simulates the entire workflow from quantum circuit definition to final execution.
key_observables: End-to-end performance metrics including entanglement-resource dynamics, fidelity, communication overhead, entanglement-resource utilization, and Job Execution Time (JET).
important_parameters: Hardware noise parameters such as qubit properties, gate errors, coherence times, readout errors, and network latency/impairments.
main_assumptions: The framework assumes the ability to model cross-layer interactions between quantum computation layers and optical networking layers.

paper_structure: The paper introduces GsOQDC, detailing its architecture which unifies circuit modeling, optical networking design (via a GUI), compilation, scheduling, and execution simulation using DES/Monte Carlo methods to evaluate cross-layer performance.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it provides a crucial simulation tool for understanding the practical architectural limitations of scaling quantum computation by explicitly coupling quantum circuit requirements with realistic optical network constraints.

figures.caption: Fig. 1: GsOQDC workflow and software architecture. The platform integrates the end-to-end DQC workflow, enabling users to progress from quantum-circuit design and optical-network configuration to distributed compilation, scheduling, execution, and performance evaluation within a single graphical environment.

Fig. 2: GsOQDC Network Designer. (a) Interactive topology editor for constructing Optical Quantum Data Center architectures using QPUs, optical components, and communication links. (b) Component configuration panel, accessible via right-click, allowing users to modify hardware and noise parameters, including qubit properties, gate errors, coherence times, readout errors, and device-specific calibration data. Together, these capabilities enable realistic, cross-layer modeling of distributed quantum-computing infrastructures.

Fig. 3: Distributed-workload scheduling in GsOQDC. (a) Interactive Gantt-chart visualization showing local operations, remote-gate execution, and communication events across multiple QPUs. (b) Contextual information panel displayed when hovering over a scheduled operation, providing timing, duration, resource, and process details. (c) User-configurable gate and process timing parameters.
